newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end with hefty gains, off peaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end with hefty gains, off peaks.

text.p: A session of high-volume trading left U.S. debt futures with hefty gains but off day's peaks.

Traders said locals gained control in the U.S. Treasury bond futures pit into the close, evening up positions before the weekend after the morning's initial bump up and subsequent grind higher that featured huge dealer and hedge fund action.

They said the weaker-than-expected U.S. consumer price and retail sales data for August had congealed sentiment that the Federal Reserve had less reason to hike interest rates by 25 basis points at the September 24 policymaking meeting.

The August consumer price index firmed 0.1 percent overall and in the core rate, versus forecasts for 0.2-percent gains in each gauge. Retail sales gained 0.2 percent overall and without autos, far lower than forecasts for up 0.7 percent overall and up 0.4 percent ex-autos.

The ensuing rally had the short end pricing back out a quarter-point tightening this month, although the December Eurodollar futures still left open the question of whether the central bank might raise rates before yearend.
But comments by Fed governor Lawrence Lindsey unsettled some traders.
"You've got to say it was a strong close," said a T-bond futures floor broker. "As long as we closed above 108-18/32, I like them."
She said that although the contract might retrace down to as low as 108-00 early next week, she expected it to head higher again nearterm.
Traders said the runup was powered by huge hedge fund and dealer buying, with one dealer seen buying as many as 6,000 December T-bonds and others executing similar-sized trades.
"All I know is, every hedge fund in America covered its shorts," she added. "You should have seen the (buy) stops."

At settlement, December T-bonds surged 1-15/32 to 108-23/32, T-notes rallied 30/32 to 107-01/32, muni-bonds jumped 1-18/32 to 113-20/32, December Eurodollars jumped 14 basis points to 94.13, and T-bills also rose 14 to 94.73. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
Lindsey told a Japanese wire service that the U.S. economy is still robust and inflation is in a dangerous zone.

"The way you saw the market react (to economic data), I'd say a lot of the Street is not looking for tightening, although Lindsey's comments makde some people doubt themselves," said a Eurodollar floor broker.
December Treasury bond futures' ability settle above 108-18/32 impressed technicians.
The 108-16/32 level represented a one-half retracement of the move from the August 13 high at 111-26/32 to last Friday's low of 105-09/32.
